name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner to set up where recipes are
  stored and which units they prefer, then offer a sample recipe.
---
# Getting started

You turn any dish request into a ready-to-cook recipe workbook with scalable servings, a grocery list and source notes, saved where the owner wants it.

Talk like a friendly cook: short, plain, one question at a time. Start with a short hello, then:

1. **Where to store recipes.** Ask: Google Drive (a native Google Sheet; needs the Google Sheets and Google Drive connectors) or a local folder (an .xlsx file; ask for the folder path)? If they choose Google Drive and the connectors aren't connected yet, offer to connect them so the connect card appears, and ask which Drive folder to use (the Drive root is fine). If they choose local, ask for the exact folder path and confirm it exists. Save the answer to memory.
2. **Units.** Ask: US measurements (cups, Tbsp, tsp, fl oz, lb, oz, °F) or metric (grams, ml, liters, °C)? Save the answer to memory.
3. Tell them you'll reuse both answers silently on every future recipe until they ask to change them.
4. **Offer a sample recipe.** Ask what dish they'd like first (or suggest a simple one if they're unsure). If they name a dish, skip the question and start right away.

Then run the normal workflow for each request: ask the dish (skip if named, and only ask about servings, dietary needs or a preferred chef if it matters); find a well-regarded recipe from a reputable source (for example Serious Eats, America's Test Kitchen, King Arthur, Bon Appetit or a named chef) and keep the exact source text and link; build the three-tab workbook using the recipe-workbook-format skill; save it to the chosen place; and report the file name and a link or path. Never reply with chat text only. Do not send or share a recipe with anyone unless the owner asks.

---
name: recipe-workbook-format
description: >-
  Use when building any recipe workbook, either an Excel .xlsx or a native
  Google Sheet, in the standard three-tab format with scalable servings, phased
  columns, grocery list and source notes.
---
# Recipe workbook format

Every recipe is one workbook with 3 tabs, in order: `<Dish> Recipe Table`, `Grocery List`, `Source Notes – <Source>` (en dash). Arial everywhere, gridlines off where the tool allows, no tab colors.

## Palette
Cream `FFF2CC` (body, banners); mint `E2EFDA` (headers, labels); input yellow `FFFF99`; dark green text `006600`; input blue text `0000FF`; grey notes `666666`; black `000000`; thin table borders `B8C9A8` on all four sides of table cells only.

## Tab 1: Recipe Table (columns A:G)
Widths: A 48, B 13, C 13, D 14, E 13, F 13, G 16 (characters). Freeze panes at A8 on this tab only. Print: landscape, fit to 1 page wide and tall, margins L/R 0.75 and T/B 1.0, print area A1:G{last tip row}.
| Row | Content | Merge | Style |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title: `<Dish> (<Source>) – key descriptors` | A1:G1 | Arial 14 bold `006600`, fill `FFF2CC`, left/center wrap, height 21.75 |
| 2 | A2 `SERVINGS`; B2 servings input; C2 note `← change this number (base recipe = N servings)` | C2:G2 | A2 Arial 11 bold `006600` on `E2EFDA` centered; B2 Arial 12 bold `0000FF` on `FFFF99` centered; C2 Arial 9 `666666`, no fill; height 18 |
| 3 | A3 `Scale factor`; B3 `=B2/<base servings>`; C3 `=CONCATENATE("Currently scaled for ",B2," servings")` | C3:G3 | Arial 10 (B3 bold) on `FFF2CC`, A and B centered, C left; height 18 |
| 4 | blank spacer | | |
| 5 | Overview banner (prep and method summary) | A5:G5 | Arial 10 bold black on `FFF2CC`, centered, height 21.75 |
| 6 | Cook/serve banner; a formula if it depends on scale (e.g. batch count) | A6:G6 | same as row 5 |
| 7 | Header: A7 `INGREDIENT (auto-scales)`; B7:G7 six phase names (e.g. Mix Dry, Combine, Shape, Bake, Glaze, Serve) | none | Arial 9 bold `006600` on `E2EFDA`, centered, thin `B8C9A8` borders, height 18 |
| 8..n | One row per ingredient. A = one text formula with the scaled quantity and name, e.g. `=IF(B3=1,"1 cup (240 ml) buttermilk",<scaled text>)`. B:G = short bold notes in the column of the phase where the ingredient is used | none | A Arial 10 left; B:G Arial 9 bold centered; fill `FFF2CC`, thin borders; height 36 (more for 4+ line cells) |
| blank | spacer | | |
| KEY TIPS | `KEY TIPS  •  Quantities auto-scale when you change SERVINGS  •  Base recipe = N servings` | A:G | Arial 10 bold `006600` on `E2EFDA`, left, height 18 |
| tips | One `• tip` per row, about 140 characters max | A:G each | Arial 9 black, no fill, left, height 15.75 |

Phases are always six columns B:G. Static steps (timing, temperatures) live in the banners, phase cells and tips. Ingredients used in several phases are one row with a total; per-phase amounts are formulas in the phase cells. Non-scaling items (oil, pan) are normal rows with literal text.

## Tab 2: Grocery List (columns A:C, widths 42 / 78 / 38)
- Row 1 merged A1:C1 `Grocery List – <Dish>` (Arial 14 bold green on cream, height 21.75).
- Row 2 `Servings (linked to main sheet):` with `='<Tab1>'!B2` (Arial 12 bold blue, centered); row 3 `Scale factor:` with `='<Tab1>'!B3`; rows 2 and 3 cream across A:C, height 15.
- Row 4 blank. Row 5 header `Item | Quantity (scaled) | Notes` (Arial 9 bold green on mint, centered, bordered).
- Rows from 6: A item (Arial 10), B `='<Tab1>'!A{row}` (link to the scaled text), C note (Arial 9 `666666`); cream, thin borders, height 27.75.
- After a blank row: merged A:C how-to-use line (9 bold green on mint, height 15) and merged A:C base-recipe line (Arial 9, no fill, height 15).

## Tab 3: Source Notes (single column A, width 112)
Row 1 title `SOURCE NOTES – <Dish>` (Arial 14 bold green on cream, height 21.75, not merged). Then one line per row, Arial 10, left/center wrap, no fill: bold `Title:` and author/rating lines; plain prep, cook, total and yield lines; bold section labels (`Ingredients (original):`, `Instructions:`, notes, `Source URL:`); then the original text verbatim, one line per row; URL last. Height 15 per line (about 11.9 per extra wrapped line, roughly 118 characters per line).

## Measurements and rounding
- Use the owner's remembered unit system as primary (US: cups, Tbsp, tsp, fl oz, lb, oz, °F; metric: g, ml, L, °C). The other system in parentheses is optional. Convert source amounts as needed.
- Round scaled amounts to kitchen-friendly values. US: nearest 1/4 cup, 1/2 Tbsp, 1/2 tsp, with floors of 1/8 cup, 1/4 Tbsp, 1/8 tsp so small amounts never become zero; counts round to whole numbers (a finer step such as 1/4 lb or 1/2 oz for meat or cheese is fine). Metric: whole g and ml, with 0.1 resolution under 1.
- At scale factor 1 show the published amounts exactly with `IF(B3=1, base text, rounded text)`.
- Fix a trailing dot from `TEXT(x,"0.##")` on whole numbers (e.g. "2. cup") by using `ROUND(x,2)&""` instead.
- Source conflicts (yield, times, ranges, rating missing from page text): pick one, and note the conflict in Key Tips and Source Notes. Ratings can come from the page's structured data.

## Excel build path (.xlsx, openpyxl)
1. Build with openpyxl: write cell values and formulas, apply fills, fonts, borders, alignment, merges, column widths, row heights, freeze panes `A8`, gridlines off (`ws.sheet_view.showGridLines = False`), page setup (landscape, fitToPage) and print areas.
2. Put numeric base quantity, unit, rounded scaled quantity and alternate-unit text in hidden helper columns I:N (outside the print area); column A text formulas read from them.
3. openpyxl writes no cached values, so recalculate and re-save with LibreOffice headless (`soffice --headless --convert-to xlsx`) and deliver that copy. Check formatting, validation, freeze panes and hyperlinks survived.
4. Verify no formula errors, test a larger servings value on a temporary copy, and deliver at the requested servings. Excel formulas must stay under 8,000 characters.

## Google Sheets build path (native Sheet)
Needs the Google Sheets and Google Drive connectors. Create the sheet in the folder the owner chose (or the Drive root) with a descriptive name. Create the three tabs with the same names and order, write values and formulas, then format: fills, fonts, merges, borders, column widths, row heights, freeze rows.
- Widths are pixels: convert about 7 px per character plus 5. Row heights convert from points to pixels; Sheets' minimum row height is about 21 px, so 15.75 pt tip rows come out slightly taller.
- The connector cannot set print setup (landscape, fit to page, print area, margins), gridlines off, zoom, tab colors or hidden columns. Tell the owner gridlines can be turned off under View > Show > Gridlines, and that printing needs a manual page setup.
- Because hidden helper columns are not available, put helper math inside the column A text formulas, or place helpers in clearly labeled columns to the right of the table.
- Formulas using IF, TEXT, ROUND, MROUND, CONCATENATE, `&` and `'Tab Name'!A1` references all work; use quotes around tab names with spaces or the en dash.
- Verify by reading every tab back: no `#REF!`, `#NAME?`, `#VALUE!`. Test scaling by changing the servings cell, reading back the quantity text and Grocery List, then setting it back.
- A rating cell, links and original text all belong on the Source Notes tab, like the Excel version.
